symptom: `mxcli check -p --references` of one `create or modify microflow` took 0.8 s on a project of 5,373 units, and most of it was reading every microflow of the project (mendixlabs/mxcli#1842, ako/mxcli#2160).
cause: check's tiers (flow verdicts, flow access, entity-access calls) each hold their own CacheUnitReads span. The span ends with the tier, the content cache is dropped, and the next tier reads every flow again -- from the persisted unit store, so `unit_file_reads` stayed 0 and nothing counted it. 454 reads on the 369-unit fixture.
fix: One CacheUnitReads span over the whole check, which writes nothing; the tiers' spans nest in it. 454 -> 278 reads on the fixture; 0.81 s -> 0.71 s for 5 statements and 2.85 s -> 2.34 s for 200 on the 5,373-unit project, identical output.
insight: The count that existed (unit_file_reads) could not see this: a re-read is served by the unit store, not a file. A read counter has to count every read not served from memory, or a cache in front of the counted path hides the repeats. Also tried and dropped: reading a listing's units on several goroutines -- no measurable gain. And the local fixture carried a warm .mxcli store from in-place use, which made the first version of the test read 0 files.
test: cmd/mxcli/check_reads_each_unit_once_test.go: file reads + store hits of one check must not exceed the project's unit count; fails with 454 > 369 when the span is removed.
